config.classes_note: Four classes, each the census's own kind, unit, labor object or intersection for the entity, stated by field sources at the loci given: (1) cloudwork, online remote work through digital labour platforms (census unit and labor_object; intersection labor-producing-ai; B1 'Defining cloudwork', B4, B10, B6); (2) AI data work, the human labour behind AI (census intersection labor-producing-ai and labor_object; B1 'Data work', B9, B8, B6); (3) algorithmic management (census intersection ai-governing-labor; B1 p. 21 and threshold 4.2); (4) rating platforms against minimum labour standards (census kind and evidence_kind; B1 'The Fairwork Project', B3, B2). The census's two remaining intersections, gains-and-losses (pay: thresholds 1.1 and 1.2, B1) and worker-power (representation: thresholds 5.1 and 5.2, B1), are carried by the field in the report's own terms and are not separate string classes. The archive's instruments of labor direction bear on these classes only where an archive text applies them, and are recorded here with their loci without being applied by the composer: the Directionality of Semantic Labor (DSL, #771, AXN-02D1 line 5: 'Directionality of semantic labor measures where a synthetic system's labor flows relative to the commissioned task, across five layers (capacity, task-origin, retrieval, output, attribution)'), its directionality stack DS-6 and its extension user labor drag (#771 §8: 'When substrate output redirects the user's subsequent semantic labor into parsing, locating, and managing the substrate rather than advancing the object, the injury is upstream of the artifact and leaves no residue in it'), with the definition surface laborvector.org (#1392). Both measure a synthetic system's labor and the user's, not the labor of human workers supplying AI through platforms; none of them names Fairwork, cloudwork or platform ratings, and the census itself records lv_intersection 'none stated' for the entity. The semantic-labor line enters by reading where its texts apply semantic labor, extraction or bearing-cost to the workers of class (2) (reading.json). Aliases: 'Fairwork' (the programme and its project), 'Cloudwork Ratings/Report/Principles', the fair.work domain. 'Fair Work' as two words is not an alias: the Australian Fair Work Ombudsman, Fair Work Act 2009 and Fair Work Commission are homonyms (Wikipedia's search for 'Fairwork' returns them), and the pattern requires the closed form or a following 'work' joined. Admission by reading (§3.4): D where a deposit names the entity and says something of it; O-class where a sentence applies an archive category (semantic labor, extraction, variance-generative labor, provenance erasure, DSL) to cloudwork, to AI data work, to algorithmic management or to rating platforms against labour standards as a class; a bare list, a citation-list entry, a reference line or a cost line naming a platform is not a claim.
